newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Vilnius Bank gets ok for share split.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Vilnius Bank gets ok for share split.

text.p: Leading Lithuanian bank Vilnius Bank has got permission to carry out a split of its shares to 50 litas each from 500 litas, bank officials said on Wednesday.

Vilnius Bank is Lithuania's leading bank and recently issued $17 million of global depositary receipts (GDR), the first Baltic financial institution to make such an issue. The GDRs are listed in Luxembourg.

"We decided to split the nominal value of our shares from 500 litas to 50 litas to make them more attractive and flexible on the Lithuanian market," Vilnius Bank deputy chairman Raimondas Kutras told Reuters.
He also said that the bank wanted to lessen the difference between the value of the GDRs and the locally-quoted stocks.
The bank recently announced nine-month profits of 16 million litas, up from 11.7 million litas after six months.
